A Codex PreCompact hook saying `Managed carry-respawn is QUEUED` proves admission only. Read the owner's `psu-pty/<owner>.events.jsonl` for the subsequent `respawn-failed` outcome before attributing repeated interruptions to the Codex model or account.

On 2026-10-24, WI-6554700010027627 reproduced the same actual owner/ADV home-repair request returning HTTP 500 through 9071 and HTTP 200 through 3170. The failing body named three su.md observation headings absent from the serving renderer's SU_TILES. These were prompt/source build skew, not a missing model route. `ensureCodexHomeViaOperator` preserved the HTTP failure classification; `recycleChild` refused replacement before stopping the original child. The hook's prior queued message then remained the visible outcome.

The durable source repair in `adv/sessions.ts` recognizes only the typed `su-tiling-unsound` error and uses the verified prior launch artifact. `pinnedSuRecoveryPrompt` checks replay integrity and receipt revision; ordinary SU sessions can opt into this recovery without a selected identity. Existing selected-source recovery keeps its original defaults. Missing artifacts, tampered receipts, unrelated errors, and identity-admission failures remain refusals. Recovery returns `pinned-renderer-skew` and does not claim a new identity activation. The PTY also reports a failed home preparation to the terminal after admission, including its HTTP status.

Verification: the endpoint regression failed before the change (two failures); the endpoint and artifact suites passed 72 tests afterward. The root-cause record is EI-26878579942685306, with the owner-directed repair tracked in WI-6554700010027627. Source verification is not evidence of rollout: the normal 9071 route still failed at the measured 16:45Z request. Final recovery requires the qualified serving writer plus a real successor turn. Keep shipment separate from staging/local proof.
